acts.title: Should schools teach cooking?
text: I believe that every school should teach basic cooking.
One reason is cost: a student who can cook three cheap meals will save money for the rest of their life, and will eat better while doing it.
For example, my brother left home at eighteen without knowing how to boil an egg, and he spent most of his first year on overpriced food that made him feel terrible.
A second reason is that cooking teaches things no other lesson does — planning, timing, and dealing with something that has gone wrong.
Some people argue that there is no room left in the timetable. However, one hour a week for a single year would be enough.
In conclusion, cooking is not a hobby. It is one of the few skills every single student will definitely use.

items.r: states the opinion in one line
supports that reason with a real example
closes by restating the point more sharply

acts.title: Spoken instructions or written opinion?
text: Instructions are spoken to somebody who is watching your hands. They use imperatives, short checks and words like this and here.
An opinion paragraph is written for a reader who cannot ask questions. It names its reasons, gives evidence and answers the other side before finishing.

In conclusion, it is one of the few skills everybody will use.

tts: Today I’m going to show you how to make a light that uses no electricity, with only seven things.
The first thing you do is cut a hole in the metal sheet. You need special metal-cutters, and you need to measure carefully. Make sure you don’t cut the hole too big.
Next, rub the plastic bottle with sandpaper.
When you’ve done that, put the bottle in the hole in the metal and glue it in place.
While the glue is drying, fill the bottle with water and add ten millilitres of bleach. Then put the top on the bottle.
After you’ve done that, it’s time to go to the roof, and cut a hole the same size as the bottle.
Finally, put the bottle in the hole and add more glue to make it secure. And there you have it.

write.q: Write an opinion paragraph of about 145 words on a school subject you think should be taught (or dropped). Follow the model exactly: opinion → first reason → example → second reason → the other side answered → conclusion.
write.model: I believe that every school should teach personal finance. One reason is that almost nobody learns it at home: parents who are bad with money pass the same habits on to their children, and the cycle simply repeats. For example, a friend of mine took out a phone contract at nineteen without reading it, and spent two years paying for a device she had already lost. A second reason is that the subject is genuinely easy to teach — interest, contracts, tax and a household budget would fit into one term. Some people argue that this is the family’s job, not the school’s. However, we do not leave reading to families, and money is no less important. In conclusion, personal finance is not an extra. It is the one subject every student in the room will need within five years.

speak.q: Now do the spoken half: choose something practical you can do well and talk somebody through it, step by step, in about a minute. Use First…, The next thing you do is…, Make sure you…, Once you’ve done that… and Finally…
speak.model: Right, I’ll show you how to make proper tea. The first thing you do is boil the water — properly boiling, not almost. While it’s heating, warm the pot with a little hot water and pour it away. The next thing you do is put in one spoon per person. Make sure you don’t leave it more than four minutes, or it goes bitter. Once you’ve done that, pour it and add the milk afterwards. Finally, drink it while it’s hot.
